-- base/.brisk.yaml --
business_rules: .brisk/business-rules.md
questions:
  - id: breaks_business_rule
    text: Does this change break or alter a project business rule listed in the state?
    raise_to: medium
-- base/.brisk/business-rules.md --
# Loyalty business rules

- Points are earned at 1 point per whole dollar spent. Partial dollars never earn a point, so amounts are always rounded down.
- Staff accounts never earn points.
- A customer's points balance never goes negative: a redemption larger than the balance must fail.
- 100 points are worth one dollar of discount, and a discount from points never exceeds 50% of the order total.
- Points expire 12 months after the purchase that earned them, not after the customer's last purchase.
-- base/internal/loyalty/points.go --
package loyalty

import (
	"errors"
	"math"
	"time"
)

// Customer is a loyalty account.
type Customer struct {
	ID     string
	Staff  bool
	Points int
	Grants []Grant
}

// Grant is points earned by one purchase.
type Grant struct {
	Points int
	At     time.Time
}

// ErrInsufficient is returned when a customer redeems more points than they have.
var ErrInsufficient = errors.New("loyalty: not enough points")

// Earn adds the points for a purchase of amount dollars.
func Earn(c *Customer, amount float64, now time.Time) int {
	if c.Staff {
		return 0
	}
	pts := int(math.Floor(amount))
	c.Points += pts
	c.Grants = append(c.Grants, Grant{Points: pts, At: now})
	return pts
}

// Redeem spends points on an order and returns the discount in dollars.
func Redeem(c *Customer, points int, orderTotal float64) (float64, error) {
	if points > c.Points {
		return 0, ErrInsufficient
	}
	discount := float64(points) / 100
	if limit := orderTotal * 0.5; discount > limit {
		discount = limit
	}
	c.Points -= points
	return discount, nil
}

// Expired reports whether grant g has expired at now.
func Expired(c *Customer, g Grant, now time.Time) bool {
	return now.After(g.At.AddDate(1, 0, 0))
}
-- base/internal/loyalty/points_test.go --
package loyalty

import (
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestEarnRoundsDown(t *testing.T) {
	c := &Customer{}
	if got := Earn(c, 9.99, time.Now()); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d", got)
	}
}
-- head/internal/loyalty/points.go --
package loyalty

import (
	"errors"
	"math"
	"time"
)

// Customer is a loyalty account.
type Customer struct {
	ID     string
	Staff  bool
	Points int
	Grants []Grant
}

// Grant is points earned by one purchase.
type Grant struct {
	Points int
	At     time.Time
}

// ErrInsufficient is returned when a customer redeems more points than they have.
var ErrInsufficient = errors.New("loyalty: not enough points")

// Earn adds the points for a purchase of amount dollars.
func Earn(c *Customer, amount float64, now time.Time) int {
	if c.Staff {
		return 0
	}
	pts := int(math.Ceil(amount))
	c.Points += pts
	c.Grants = append(c.Grants, Grant{Points: pts, At: now})
	return pts
}

// Redeem spends points on an order and returns the discount in dollars.
func Redeem(c *Customer, points int, orderTotal float64) (float64, error) {
	if points > c.Points {
		return 0, ErrInsufficient
	}
	discount := float64(points) / 100
	if limit := orderTotal * 0.5; discount > limit {
		discount = limit
	}
	c.Points -= points
	return discount, nil
}

// Expired reports whether grant g has expired at now.
func Expired(c *Customer, g Grant, now time.Time) bool {
	return now.After(g.At.AddDate(1, 0, 0))
}
